DONATE

Home » Jazz Articles » Album Review » Kate Williams: On The Wing Of A Dragonfly

 LIKE 4
Kate Williams: On The Wing Of A Dragonfly
By Neil Duggan
May 23, 2026
View read count
One of the many pleasures of a piano trio is that the pianist is freed from the need to complement or integrate with other harmonic voices, breathing more expansively, leaving gaps in the texture or venturing into unexpected tonal areas. The bass also benefits from this openness: it steps into sharper relief, freed from a reinforcing role to reveal its melodic character and tonal weight.

Composer and pianist Kate Williams has a playing style ideally suited to take advantage of this openness on her album On The Wings Of A Dragonfly. Her patient, unhurried approach is reflected in her compositions; they evolve gradually and with clear purpose, supported by her trusted long-term collaborators, bassist Oli Hayhurst and drummer David Ingamells.

Williams has more often been heard in quartet, quintet, or much larger ensembles. The trio format affords her greater freedom while leaving the playing and improvisation more exposed, but she revels in the space, producing eight compositions alongside a Fats Waller cover.

The title track bookends the album. Both versions unfold gradually, spreading out from piano motifs that climb and fall. The band interplay is relaxed and assured. On the opening track this leads to a feature for Hayhurst before the trio make their way back to the main melody. The two versions are similar, but the closing track is more chilled and misses the bass solo.

Williams often uses repetitive phrases, sometimes introducing slight changes to tease out the theme. "Soon Enough" uses this structure as it builds through a fine bass solo, arriving at a swinging, flowing melody. "In Sight" follows a similar line with the pianist showing more of a Thelonious Monk influence, which develops into another compelling solo.

The one cover version, Waller's "Jitterbug Waltz," is a sheer delight. The classic tune is reinterpreted for contemporary audiences with inventive rhythmic interplay while maintaining the captivating descending keyboard line. There is more excitement on the bop-flavored "Taker's Dozen," which sounds like a classic from yesteryear, as Williams adds sparkle with her quick-witted phrasing, supported by Ingamells' brisk and bustling drumming and a terrific solo from Hayhurst.

Elsewhere, the tense atmosphere of "A Rose-Tinted Spectacle" is heightened by a gripping crescendo from Ingamells, while the delightful "Snowdrops To Wintersweet" offers seven minutes of reflective calm. Williams' compositions are meticulously crafted to draw out the strengths of her trio, their collective chemistry shifting effortlessly between improvised and composed sections. The album's trio setting, alongside the superb recording quality, allows Williams to display her radiant piano skills to compelling effect.
Track Listing

On The Wing Of A Dragonfly; Soon Enough; A Rose-Tinted Spectacle; In Sight; Snowdrops To Wintersweet; Taker's Dozen; Short Order; Jitterbug Waltz; On The Wing Of A Dragonfly (reprise).

Home » Jazz Articles » Album Review » Faye Carrol: Forever Dynamic

 LIKE 2
Faye Carrol: Forever Dynamic
By Pierre Giroux
May 23, 2026
View read count
Faye Carol has never been a singer who tiptoes into a song. On Forever Dynamic, she strides straight into the centre of each tune, claims it, and leaves her fingerprints all over it. Twenty tracks across 2 CDs might seem like a lot on paper, but in Carol's hands, it plays like one long set, with the band locked in and nobody watching the clock. Those hardy collaborators along for the ride include pianist and musical director Joe Warner, bassist Tarus Mateen, and drummer Dennis Chambers, who plays on all tracks, with Dante Robertson on one track.

Carol opens with "Hello, Young Lovers" from the 1951 Rodgers and Hammerstein Broadway musical The King and I. But do not expect them in white tie and tails. Carol and Warner set the table with a bluesy groove, teasing the melody in her quivering voice. Warner's touch keeps the ears alert, while Mateen and Chambers add just enough snap to keep the number in funky motion. "Can't Take My Eyes Off You," by Bob Crewe and Bob Gaudio, was a big hit for Frankie Valli, but Carol reshapes it here. In this slow-burning confession, her voice opens up in the chorus with a sense of urgency.

On Dizzy Gillespie's "Groovin' High," the gloves come off, and her bebop agility is on full display. She darts through the changes with precision and a playful sense of risk. It is not just technique but pure joy. Warner dashes across the keyboard with proficiency, and the rhythm section is pugnacious and resourceful. Carol slides into "Nature Boy" with a confident stride, taking the lead from Mateen's plucking. As the number unfolds, she shades the mysticism with a blues undercurrent. The song feels less like a parable and more like a testimony.

Irving Gordon wrote "Unforgettable," popularized by Nat King Cole on his 1951 release. Carol takes the number up a notch with a Latin-funky vibe that delivers a soulful declaration. Carol tackles "Hard Times Won't Last" with a blend of gospel inflection and blues phrasing. There is weight here, but also resilience, which permeates the album.

The Billie Holiday classic "Fine and Mellow" raises the temperature. Chambers locks into a backbeat that harkens to the tune's antecedents without sounding dated. Carol digs into the lyric with grit and strut.

The album closes with "I Rise, I Rise, Still I Rise," adapted from a poem by Maya Angelou and set to music by Carol and Warner. Delivered with dignity and quiet power. Carol's voice is weathered but resolute and unmistakably her own, completing the arc.

items.body: Hans Zimmer is set to return to Singapore with his brand-new live production, Hans Zimmer Live – The Next Level World Tour 2026, happening on 7 October at the Singapore Indoor Stadium. Presented by AEG Presents Asia, Semmel Concerts, and RCI Global, the upcoming show marks the legendary composer’s first performance in Singapore since 2019. Known for transforming film scores into immersive live spectacles, Zimmer’s latest production promises an even more ambitious cinematic experience, featuring electronic sound design, large-scale orchestration, spectacular lighting, and a brand-new stage concept. View this post on Instagram A post shared by AEG Presents Asia (@aegpresentsasia) Speaking about the tour, Zimmer shared: “I want fans to feel like they’re at a rave party or riding a roller coaster. For me, every show is a new voyage of discovery.” Fans can expect fresh arrangements from some of Zimmer’s most iconic film scores, including music from Pirates of the Caribbean, The Lion King, The Dark Knight, Interstellar, and Dune. The setlist will also feature selections from Dune: Part Two and F1®: The Movie. View this post on Instagram A post shared by AEG Presents Asia (@aegpresentsasia) The Singapore stop is part of Zimmer’s wider Asia run, which will also see the composer perform in cities such as Yokohama, Kaohsiung, Taipei, Beijing, Hangzhou, Chengdu, and Guangzhou. Tickets will go on sale via SISTIC on 2 June from 10 AM onwards.

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Let's just be honest here, does anyone actually go out of their way to listen to this album? The thing is, it's not bad, it's just, well? weird. 'Time Requiem', a progressive metal band specializing in lightning-fast flurries of notes in a neoclassical vein, is the product of keyboard mastermind Richard Andersson. They'd only released one studio album prior to this, so like? why produce a live album so early in their career?It just seems unusual. I don't know a lot about the band, but I would take a guess that, like other, similar groups, they probably don't gig very often, if ever. And with a limited choice of songs, it just doesn't really offer much for the listener to sink their teeth into. For what it's worth though, the performances are fantastic. Each member of the band plays with machine-like precision. The sound is very good, and the crowd seem quite receptive to the band, though my guess is that this isn't typically a Time Requiem audience. It could also just be that I've always preferred studio albums to their live counterparts. But overall, this isn't a bad release, but I doubt I'll ever listen to it again. I'll just stick to the bands studio output instead.

items.body: This overall limited run of the acid genre is another success on the label for those who are in love with the genre. Furthur Electronix—and a warm welcome Shakesphere, their sub-label—has been carving out a niche for itself over the past few years, releasing music that feels both nostalgic and necessary. It’s a love letter to a sound that defined an era, and for fans of classic acid and braindance, it’s essential. An excellent braindance outing that pulls directly from the classic acid playbook Italian maestro SRS returns on the Furthur Electronix offshoot Shakesphere with Plastic EP, an excellent braindance outing that pulls directly from the classic acid playbook. Furthur Electronix, a Brighton-based label founded by Anil Lal, Jay Lal, and graphic designer Majkel, has built a reputation for releasing high-quality electronic music: techno, deep house, IDM, electro, and acid, on limited vinyl pressings, often restricted to 200 copies. The label’s aesthetic leans heavily on Warp, Rephlex, and Skam influences, and Plastic EP is no exception. This release is a limited run on vinyl distributed through Clone, and it brings some weight to it from a remix by D’Arcangelo. While the main tracks “Plastic 1” and “Plastic 2” are acid in nature, the acid breaks here remain on the classic front of other acid artists. Acid house emerged in the mid-80s with Chicago producers like Phuture, DJ Pierre, and Spanky using the Roland TB-303 bass synthesizer to create squelchy, hypnotic basslines that defined a generation of dance music. By the early 90s, acid had crossed over into the UK rave scene and found a home on labels like Rephlex, where artists like AFX (Aphex Twin), Universal Indicator, and Mike Dred pushed the sound into more abstract and experimental territory. The TB-303’s signature sound—resonant, modulated, and aggressive, became a staple of the braindance movement. Plastic EP doesn’t reinvent that sound. It honors it. Both “Plastic 1” and “Plastic 2” have a great vibe to them, and it’s understood why such a sound in this genre would be released on a limited run, the genre within itself feels classic, like a direct transmission from 1993. “Plastic 1” is my favorite over the bunch. It has a more darker, heavier acid sound, bringing back the old acid days. 4/4 kicks and heavy acid rhythms mix in with shuffled hats throughout. No melodies here, but the acid serves it well with its teases of acid rhythms. The TB-303 is doing all the heavy lifting, modulating and shifting across the track’s runtime, and the production is raw but not lo-fi. It’s clean enough to hit hard on a club system but dirty enough to retain that gritty, analog charm. The D’Arcangelo remix brings a different vibe—still acid, but more dancier and with an electro edge, which is what their style is known for. D’Arcangelo, the Italian duo of brothers Fabrizio and Marco D’Arcangelo, have been active in the underground electronic scene since the early 90s. Their 1996 debut on Rephlex is considered a classic, fusing fierce, industrial-strength electronix with playful, melodic synthpop. I expected more of their experimental IDM style, but the drums here are very well implemented along with the transitional effects on the drum beats. The remix doesn’t stray too far from the original’s acid core, but it adds movement and groove, pulling it closer to the dancefloor without sacrificing the edge. “Third Eye” seems to be more on the softer ambient side of things and sounds completely different from the rest of the EP. I see it as a good alternative—still acid sounds in it, but more subtle. The TB-303 is there, but it’s restrained, sitting beneath layers of pads and atmospheric textures. It’s a comedown track, a moment of breath after the intensity of “Plastic 1” and “Plastic 2.” This overall limited run of the acid genre is another success on the label for those who are in love with the genre. Furthur Electronix—and a warm welcome Shakesphere, their sub-label—has been carving out a niche for itself over the past few years, releasing music that feels both nostalgic and necessary. It’s a love letter to a sound that defined an era, and for fans of classic acid and braindance, it’s essential. Plastic is available on Shakesphere / Furthur Electronix on June 15, 2026. [Clone]
items._cn_summary: Shakesphere子厂牌发行的这张Acid风格EP延续了Furthur Electronix厂牌对复古Braindance声音的坚持。意大利艺术家SRS带来两首Acid作品，采用标志性的TB-303音色，呈现致敬式的创作立场。《Plastic 1》以暗黑沉重的Acid线条和4/4节拍见长，制作保持干净又不失模拟质感；D'Arcangelo的混音版则融入更多Electro元素和舞曲化处理。整体而言是acid house类型中扎实的小众发行，限量200张的独立厂牌发行方式符合其地下定位。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the many progressive Spanish acts that flourished after the collapse of the Franco regime,ENBOR was one of the more folk based groups that emerged from the Basque region in Spain'snortheastern corner. This band was formed in the city of Bilbao in 1978 and existed for three yearsin which time it managed to release two progressive folk rock albums beginning with this eponymouslytitled debut which came out in 1979. While one of the mellower bands on the scene, ENBOR (whichseems to mean "tree trunk") featured a rather large lineup which included Joxe Portela (vocals,acoustic guitar), Ram�n Gardeazabal (vocals, acoustic guitar), Manu Urretxaga (vocals, saxophone,clarinet, flute), Amaia Kareaga (vocals), I�aki Arnal (bass, 1978-79), Javi Robador (drums), I�akiGutierrez (vocals, guitar). The band experienced a slightly modified lineup for the second album.Like similarly minded Basque acts, ENBOR also structured its songs around the melodic features ofthe local folk music as well as singing in the Basque language which features a completely differentrhythmic vibe from the Spanish language. The album featured seven tracks and only added up to about33 minutes of playing time. The band delivers a very straightforward style of melodic folk thatfeatured rock instrumentation along with touches of soft jazz. Also typical of the region, ENBOReschewed any of the characteristics of the Rock Andaluz craze that was rocking the rest of Spainduring the late 1970s. The tracks are light and breezy and built around strong melodies and tight-knit vocal harmonies with softer rock attributes such as mid tempos, a folky gentleness and lots ofclarinet, flute and the occasional saxophone presence. While compared to contemporary acts such as Itoiz, Haizea or Oskorri, ENBOR was the leastprogressive of the lot and only featured minor prog elements that were a secondary feature to themusic's main aim of crafting sing-songy folk rock songs. The only time progressive elements areintroduced are in the instrumental parts and then only barely flickering into the prog lite mode.Possible comparisons from other parts of Europe could be made with bands like Mellow Candle,Fairport Convention or the British Folk Revival band only steeped with local Basque flavors ratherthan the more Anglicized styles that found their way into many folk lexicons around Europe. Thealbum is fairly consistent without any surprises to be found. The music exudes a dreamy cloudcovered spring afternoon in some undisclosed woodlands and unlike anything the rather hideous albumcover art may insinuate.Overall it's a pleasant slice of slightly progified Basque folk rock in good taste with no tracksneither sounding lackluster nor particularly memorable. It's just a well presented folk rock stylefrom a nook of the European continent that gives it a touch of an exotic flair given that the Basquelanguage is a true isolate unrelated to any other European language. For those seeking the most progoriented of acts from the region then this one will surely disappoint as the prog characteristicsare rather slim and personally i would barely qualify this album as prog folk at all but it doesfeature a few more elements that would allow it to just squeak by as such. For those seeking themore authentic Basque folk expressions then this one will satisfy on that front as some of theproggier hybrid acts tended to dilute the homegrown flavors in favor of adopting prog aspectsimported from other lands. A beautifully performed album but nothing on here stands out as exemplaryor the least bit essential either.
items._cn_summary: ENBOR是1979年来自西班牙巴斯克地区的 progressive folk rock 乐队，使用与西班牙语截然不同的巴斯克语演唱，音乐以旋律优美的民谣为基础，融合软爵士元素。乐队编制较大，使用单簧管、长笛和萨克斯风等木管乐器，呈现轻快优雅的民谣摇滚风格。评论指出其prog元素极为有限，仅在器乐部分有所体现，属于巴斯克地区folk rock中「进步性最低」的乐队，与英国民谣复兴风格有一定相似之处。音乐整体流畅悦耳但缺乏突破性实验元素，对于偏好实验/前卫或爵士的用户而言吸引力有限，但巴斯克语作为语言孤岛的独特文化背景为作品增添了一定的世界音乐价值。

items.body: Review by The Progolyte — Gleemen was one of the first Rock Progressivo Italiano groups to ever come out, with their one and only record of the seventies, their self-titled, coming out all the way back in 1970. I obviously got attracted to this record from its very strange album cover, which depicts some sort of creature being killed and stabbed by various other creatures and is an ugly yet captivating piece of art. Moving on, while this band is listed as Rock Progressivo Italiano on ProgArchives, it's more or less just trippy hard rock with some symphonic textures added to it, with minimal details going beyond just a few cool riffs and a slightly interesting rhythm sections and various solos. One of the main things I didn't like about this record was the vocals, which on my first listen I thought sounded a lot like what Garybaldi was doing in their albums, and I thought it was just a coincidence until I noticed that the two bands were actually related and shared some of the same personnel (it's actually basically the same personnel as Garybaldi in the seventies. Moving on to the music, so with the band being related to Garybaldi, you can obviously tell that there will be some similarities to their music. Now, it's not that I dislike Garybaldi, I just think they're a B-tier band, so I was thinking the I Gleemen would be the same once I found out they were essentially the same band, just with a different name and in different years. And I was right. The music here is quite bland and doesn't have very many good details and is quite simple and normal in the grand scheme of things when you look at the Rock Progressivo Italiano bands that would come out in the following years. Now don't get me wrong, I do respect Gleemen for being one of the first Italian bands to release an album exploring this musical direction and something similar to the classic heavier symphonic prog sound of Rock Progressivo Italiano, they just lack the energy, excitement, depth, and complexity of others. However, some of the music here was still memorable and had some nice touches that made it flow nicely. In conclusion, Gleemen will most likely remain as the forgotten origins of Garybaldi and never get any big recognition within the progressive rock community (or even in the Rock Progressivo Italiano community), but at least they tried, and the one album they put out was alright. This one is a mid 3/5.
items._cn_summary: Gleemen是1970年意大利前卫摇滚的早期尝试，属于传统摇滚框架，融入了一定的迷幻与交响元素。该专辑在意大利摇滚史上具有先驱意义，但音乐结构相对简单，缺乏深度和复杂性，未能充分展现实验性与创新性。编曲中虽有可辨识的riff和节奏段落，但整体表现平淡，未能突破传统摇滚的窠臼。对于偏好实验与前卫风格的用户而言，该作品与实验/电子/爵士等方向距离较远，接近主流摇滚范畴。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — Here is the latest offering from European progressive rock trio Lunear, who are comprised of JP Benadjer (guitars, bass, vocals), Seb Bournier (drums, vocals) and Paul J. No (lead vocals, keyboards). I have not always been the biggest fan of their output, but there is no doubt that 2024's 'From Above' was a huge step in the right direction, and here we find them making another change which is massively positive. There are a couple of longer numbers here, but in reality, this release is all about highly melodic songs where crossover sometimes moves into neo, while the harmonies are reminiscent of the softer forms of American AOR.It is an album filled with light and sunshine as the trio continue to progress on the musical journey they commenced in 2018, with this being their fifth album to date, and is a million miles away from the album of covers they released in 2022 of which I was certainly not a fan. This is easy listening prog, but that is not to say it is not worth discovering as there are times when it is nice to move away from the heavy ego of some prog acts and instead turn to something which is middle of the road and still very enjoyable and pleasant on the ears. This style of progressive rock may be too simplistic for some, but I confess I think this has some really good songs, especially when they turn it up and increase the tempo on the likes of "I'll Remember This" as that is a power pop/prog rocker which should be released as a single and aimed at the charts!Lunear continue to delight and surprise, and I wonder what the next album will bring. This is an album where the listener can just have fun and not contort their ears into knots attempting to understand what is going on.
items._cn_summary: 欧洲前卫摇滚三人乐团Lunear的第五张专辑，定位为跨界前卫摇滚，强调高度旋律化的歌曲创作，和声处理借鉴美国柔和AOR风格。评论者将其定义为轻松聆听式的前卫摇滚，属于中庸路线，缺乏实验性探索和复杂编曲，节奏处理较为平易近人。专辑融入新古典元素但未形成独特的艺术视角，整体风格偏向主流听众。对于偏好实验性和前卫创新的用户而言，该作品过于简单直接，缺少能够吸引其注意力的创新元素或跨界融合。

items.body: Im Kino zu weinen hat etwas wunderbar Befreiendes. Erst mag es sich cheesy anfühlen, im Kollektiv die Tränen laufen zu lassen, doch irgendwann beginnt ein heilsamer Prozess. In Joachim Triers Familiendrama Sentimental Value hallte das Schluchzen unzählige Male von der hintersten Reihe bis zur Leinwand. Und auch Wochen später durchlebt man dank Hania Ranis Soundtrack diese Emotionen im heimischen Wohnzimmer noch einmal. Aufgenommen in den ikonischen Abbey Road Studios und in der originalen Filmlocation des Familienhauses in Oslo, erzählen die zehn Pianostücke die berührende Geschichte ihrer zerrütteten Figuren auf zarte und unpathetische Weise. Während Musik und Charaktere im Film beinahe miteinander verschmelzen, rufen die nach den Protagonist:innen benannten Kompositionen beim erneuten Hören klare Erinnerungen an sie hervor. So pirscht sich das Klavier in »Agnes« wie die ruhigere der beiden Schwestern leise und zaghaft heran und lässt einzelne Töne länger verweilen. Die akzentuierten Akkorde und nachdenklichen Pausen in »Nora« wiederum spiegeln die Zerbrechlichkeit und Ambivalenz der mit Lampenfieber kämpfenden Schauspielerin. Das ihr gewidmete Stück wirkt als Abschluss des Albums wie eine Versöhnung mit dem gemeinsamen Vater Gustav, der ungewollt ein generationenübergreifendes Trauma weiterträgt. Hörbar wird diese düstere Vergangenheit durch beunruhigende, ätherische Klänge, die wie ein eisiger Wind durchs Stereo ziehen.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张配合Joachim Trier家庭剧情片的电影原声专辑，由波兰钢琴家Hania Rani创作。专辑收录十首以片中角色命名的钢琴曲，在Abbey Road Studios和奥斯陆实景录制。评论聚焦于音乐与角色的情感对应，如《Agnes》的轻柔细腻、《Nora》反映的脆弱与矛盾，以及终曲与父亲创伤的和解。整体呈现简洁的钢琴独奏形式，融入些许氛围音景，属于较为传统的电影配乐风格。对于偏好实验、前卫或电子音乐的用户而言，钢琴原声与电影配乐的定位匹配度不高，音乐语言偏向当代古典而非创新跨界，波兰背景可作为地区加分项，但不足以显著提升整体评价。

items.body: Zen As Fuck is release number three from the lo-fi/outsider folk project King Futile. Behind it is Lea Cummings (Kylie Minoise, Official Music Team, etc.) . The album takes in eight tracks, featuring basic strummed-yet-enduring structures, with the lyrics being decidedly sweary, morosely comic, and sarcastic. The album appears on Lea's own label, Kovorox Sound. It comes in the form of a CDR, with artwork similar to the project's other albums- in a photocopied sleeve, with white Sharpie writing against a grey backdrop. We go from crude strumming blues & billowing singing of "Fears" where Lea lists various types of phobias like thunder, numbers, cheese, sunlight, before concluding he's not 'Fucking scared of you'. There's the slow 'n' steady strum of "Staying in Bed", where he sings about possibly climbing Everest or getting rid of poverty; instead, he'll sleep in bed dreaming everyone is dead. On "Columbo" he roughly warbles & semi croons out the track's title over very slowed/ almost staggering to a stop strum fest. And on the instrumental track "Zelda 3" we find a selection of gloomy, at times almost discordant tumblings. Zen As Fuck follows the sonic tone & lyrical feel of the first two King Futile , but with maybe a slightly more woozy to glum edge.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑属于Lo-fi/outsider folk风格，由独立小众厂牌Kovorox Sound发行。音乐采用低保真制作，吉他弹奏结构简单直接，歌词带有明显的咒骂和讽刺风格，呈现出忧郁幽默与黑色喜剧的结合。专辑包含八首曲目，涵盖蓝调元素、民谣叙事以及略带试验性的器乐段落。整体制作以CDR形式呈现，包装简朴带有手工感。考虑到用户偏好更偏向实验、前卫和跨领域融合的音乐类型，这类边缘民谣虽具有一定独立精神，但在创新性和跨界融合方面相对有限，与主流听众群体有一定距离。

items.body:
(headline image: Xara, winners of Concurso Runas 2025. The band is set to perform in the 2026 festival.)

More than 100,000 votes were registered in the 2026 edition of the Runas Contest, marking one of the event’s strongest participation totals in recent years. Organized by the Festival Internacional do Mundo Celta de Ortigueira, the competition has promoted Celtic culture and music since 2000.

This year’s results also revealed complete agreement between the public vote and the professional jury. Both selected JDC, Aérokorda, and Leni Pérez & Sekadra as the three finalists set to perform this summer at the festival.

The finalists emerged through a five-vote system. One score came from online public voting through the festival’s official website, while four additional scores came from a professional jury appointed by the festival organization. The panel evaluated each project according to its connection with the festival’s musical tradition and artistic identity.

The jury included a representative from the festival’s communications department, journalist Eva Fernández — editor of the digital magazine Rebelico and a specialist in Galician traditional culture — Pablo Martínez on behalf of the Escola de Gaitas, and Manel López, cultural officer for the Concello de Ortigueira.

The three finalists will perform on July 9 at the Estrella Galicia Stage. Afterward, a new jury selected by the festival’s organizing committee will choose the overall winner. The winning act will return to the festival in 2027 as part of the official lineup and will also appear at the 2026 Festival Internacional Sierra Celta during the town’s Medieval Days celebrations.

Madrid-based JDC, led by Jesús del Castillo, returns to the contest after winning the Runas competition in 2022. The group presents a renewed repertoire centered on strong instrumental arrangements and original compositions.

Belgian group Aérokorda brings a contemporary folk project rooted in Atlantic and Breton influences. Their live performances combine European folk traditions with modern arrangements and a lively stage approach.

Meanwhile, Leni Pérez & Sekadra unite Galician tradition with contemporary folk influences through original material that balances melodic sensitivity and live intensity.

For more information, visit Festival de Ortigueira.
items._cn_summary: Runas音乐比赛是西班牙加利西亚凯尔特民俗音乐的推广平台，本届三位决赛选手分别代表传统民俗的不同演绎路径。马德里JDC专注器乐编排与原创曲目，比利时Aérokorda将大西洋和布列塔尼传统融入现代民谣，Leni Pérez & Sekadra则平衡旋律感与现场张力。这些音乐人虽具备原创性，但整体风格仍属传统民俗范畴，缺乏实验性或跨界融合的先锋元素，与实验、前卫、电子等用户核心偏好存在较大距离。

 LIKE 4
Kate McGarry, Lenora Zenzalai Helm, Lois Deloatch, Nnenna Freelon: The Sistering
By Jacob Sylvester
May 24, 2026
View read count
The collaborative album created by jazz vocalists Kate McGarry, Lenora Zenzalai Helm, Lois Deloatch, and Nnenna Freelon, titled The Sistering, is a powerful musical journey that explores the bonds of friendship and heritage. Released in early 2026, the project uses the metaphor of "sistering"—a building technique where two boards are joined to make a structure stronger—to show how these four women support one another. The album begins with the "River Song," which introduces the idea of life as a flowing stream that connects the past to the present. This is quickly followed by "A Brother (Just Like You)," a song written and led by Freelon that honors the supportive men in their lives, showing that their community of strength extends beyond just the four vocalists. Furthermore, the album is essentially jazz with very pleasing nuances of folk, spirituals, blues, and Americana - you will enjoy this one.

As the album moves into its middle section, the themes become more serious and reflective of the struggles people face. Deloatch leads "Dying Season," a track that deals honestly with the sadness and change that comes with loss. This transition leads into "The Circle," where McGarry sings about the repetitive nature of life and how we often return to the same important lessons. Helm then takes the lead on "Begin Again," a long and beautiful piece that encourages listeners to find the courage to start over after a difficult time. These songs work together to show that even when life is hard, having a strong foundation of friends can help a person stay upright.

The later half of the album focuses on where we come from and how we balance different parts of our identity. "Origins" looks back at ancestral roots, while "Combat Boots and Glass Slippers" highlights the balance between being a strong warrior and a graceful dreamer. This track features all four women and emphasizes that they don't have to choose between being tough and being elegant. The next song, "Follow The Stream" leads into the deeply poignant "Dreaming Arms." This specific song serves as a profound remembrance of Freelon's late husband, reflecting on the "tender strands of silvery gray" and the desire to find sanctuary in the memory of his embrace. It suggests that even in the "autumn" of life and through the fog of grief, the structural support of love remains an enduring force.

Toward the end of the album, the music dives into a deep discussion of family wisdom and tradition. In "Tribal Download," McGarry describes the act of uncovering family secrets and memories as if she were walking down into a quiet cellar. The mood then shifts to a more classic sound with "It Had To Be You," a jazz standard that the group performs together to celebrate the fact that they were destined to work with each other. This song feels like a celebration of their longtime friendship and the professional respect they share as veterans of the jazz world.

The album concludes by bringing the listener back to where everything started, leaving a lasting impression of unity. The "River Song Reprise" acts as a short, peaceful harmonic ending that reminds us that the "river" of life and sisterhood never truly stops flowing. By the time the final note fades, McGarry, Helm, Deloatch, and Freelon have successfully proven that their combined voices are much more powerful than any one voice alone. The Sistering stands as a beautiful example of how art can be used to document real-life connections and provide a sense of healing, support, and inspiration to every listener.

 LIKE 4
Abbey Lincoln: That's Him
By C. Andrew Hovan
May 24, 2026
View read count
An intriguing byproduct of the current vinyl renaissance, Record Store Day has become a proving ground for labels looking to balance archival reverence with commercial opportunity. Craft Recordings has carved out a particularly compelling niche, frequently issuing mono editions of classic titles from its catalog. Following previous releases featuring Gerry Mulligan, Bill Evans, Max Roach, and Chet Baker, the label now turns its attention to Abbey Lincoln's second Riverside outing, That's Him. Cut all-analog by Kevin Gray and pressed at Fidelity Record Pressing, the release reflects the high production standards increasingly expected in today's reissue market.

Lincoln's debut adhered to the prevailing late-'50s formula, pairing vocalists with lush, string-laden arrangements. By contrast, That's Him (1958) places her squarely in a small-group jazz setting, backed by the so-called Riverside Jazz Stars. At the time, Kenny Dorham, Sonny Rollins, and Wynton Kelly were central figures in the hard bop movement and already well established on the label. Lincoln's musical and personal partnership with Roach lends the session an added charge, and the ensemble's easy rapport makes for a consistently engaging listen. Notably, this mono reissue strips away much of the echo and sonic haze that marred earlier editions, revealing a more immediate and intimate soundstage.

Rollins' robust tenor sets the tone on the opening "Strong Man," an early composition by Oscar Brown Jr. Dorham's muted trumpet provides sly interjections beneath Lincoln's long, assured vocal lines. On "Happiness Is Just a Thing Called Joe," Rollins contributes a brief but eloquent solo, while Lincoln's impeccable intonation remains front and center. The remainder of side one leans toward balladry, highlighted by a striking a cappella reading of "Tender as a Rose," where Lincoln commands complete attention, shaping each phrase with remarkable control.

Side two opens with renewed energy as Lincoln and Roach engage in a subtle dialogue on "I Must Have That Man," before the tempo lifts and both Dorham and Rollins deliver spirited statements. Paul Chambers' bowed bass introduces "Porgy," complemented by Dorham's muted lines and Lincoln's finely shaded vibrato. Rollins reveals a less frequently heard side of his playing on the blues-inflected "When a Woman Loves a Man," channeling an earthy tone reminiscent of Coleman Hawkins. The set closes with a reflective "Don't Explain," which Lincoln inhabits fully, offering a reading that stands apart from the iconic version by Billie Holiday.

Taken as a whole, this reissue not only reaffirms That's Him as a pivotal entry in Lincoln's discography, but also presents it with a clarity and presence that surpass previous editions. A cornerstone recording, now heard closer than ever to its original intent.
Track Listing

Strong Man; Happiness is Just a Thing Called Joe; My Man; Tender as a Rose; That's Him; I Must Have That Man; Porgy; When a Woman Loves a Man; Don't Explain.

 LIKE 4
Chris Coull Quartet With Imogen Ryall: Songs From Porgy And Bess
By Neil Duggan
May 24, 2026
View read count
The opera Porgy and Bess, composed by George Gershwin with lyrics by DuBose Heyward and Ira Gershwin, features many iconic songs that have crossed over into other genres, with many becoming jazz standards, while others have been covered by pop and rock artists.

Gershwin, who also composed Rhapsody in Blue and An American in Paris, poured jazz, blues, gospel and inventive orchestration into his score, creating a work that was groundbreaking for its time.

This landmark of American music has provoked controversy since its premiere with themes of domestic violence, addiction, racial representation and temptation that continue to resonate today. UK trumpeter Chris Coull sets these complexities aside, shifting the focus to bringing a vibrant selection of the opera's songs to life for contemporary audiences.

Coull draws on the original 1935 score alongside the celebrated Miles Davis and Gil Evans recording (Sony Music Entertainment, 1959), revitalizing some of the opera's most memorable moments. His quintet pays due respect to the past while keeping the focus on contemporary jazz. He is joined in this project by award-winning vocalist Imogen Ryall and an excellent rhythm section of pianist John Turville, bassist Simon Thorpe.

The album gets off to a winning start with a swinging rendition of "The Buzzard Song," Ryall's range and diction suiting the narrative style of the material perfectly. Coull's edgy trumpet interjections lead to a fine solo before he hands off to Turville. The band navigates the moody spiritual style of "Gone, Gone, Gone" before moving into a haunting version of "My Man's Gone Now," with Ryall's emotional delivery and Coull's thoughtful solo in assured balance.

All the opera's instantly recognizable songs are present. Coull's soaring trumpet punctuates the verses of the bustling drive of "It Ain't Necessarily So," while the rhythmic and light-hearted "I've Got Plenty Of Nothing" has considered phrasing that aligns with the sassy trumpet lines, complemented by Turville, Thorpe and Fishwick's impeccable support. The band stretches out on a sparkling version of "There's A Boat That's Leaving Soon For New York," which Ryall sings with a smile in her voice. Coull's perceptive solo work unfolds beautifully on "I Love You Porgy," and there is an irrepressible groove as the band has fun on "Oh Lord, I'm On My Way."

Alongside his perfectly tailored rhythm section, Coull turns in a masterful performance, as his classic bebop lines move between sensitivity and intensity. Ryall's nimble vocals continue to shine brightly across the broad range of material, delivering melancholy and joy in equal measure. Of course, one song from the opera has been covered more than most; "Summertime" is frequently the subject of impressive big band arrangements or major vocal performances. In a strikingly original short take, Ryall sings it unaccompanied, apart from gurgling baby sounds, reminding listeners that the song is a lullaby. It makes a fitting conclusion to Coull's thoroughly impressive project.
Track Listing

The Buzzard Song; Gone Gone Gone; My Man's Gone Now; Porgy I'm Your Woman Now; I've Got Plenty Of Nothing; It Ain’t Necessarily So; Prayer (Oh Dr. Jesus); Strawberry Woman - Honeyman; I Love You Porgy; There's A Boat That’s Leaving Now For New York; Oh Lord, I'm On My Way; Summertime.

items.body: South Korean indie favourites JANNABI are finally heading to Singapore for the very first time. Presented by FriedRice Entertainment, the duo’s JANNABI 1st Asia Tour : Sweat & Stardust in Singapore will take place on 13 August at Capitol Theatre, marking the Singapore stop of the band’s first-ever Asia tour. Comprised of Choi Jung-hoon and Kim Do-hyung, JANNABI have become one of Korea’s most beloved indie acts thanks to their nostalgic chamber pop sound and emotionally resonant songwriting. Since debuting in 2014, the band have steadily built a devoted following through releases that explore themes of youth, love, and growth. View this post on Instagram A post shared by FriedRice Entertainment (@friedrice.live) The band are perhaps best known for their breakout hit ‘for lovers who hesitate’, which took home Song of the Year at the 17th Korean Music Awards in 2020. Their live performances have also earned acclaim for their immersive storytelling and distinct concepts, with their futuristic concert All the Boys and Girls 2125 winning the Grand Prize for Best Concert at the 12th EDAILY Culture Awards. Fans attending the Singapore show can also look forward to exclusive fan benefits. VIP ticket holders will receive priority entry to the standing pen, priority merchandise access, a JANNABI guitar pick, and a chance to win a signed concert poster. All ticket holders will also receive a commemorative postcard. Tickets go on sale from 2 PM (SGT) on 3 June via Ticketmaster Singapore.

items.body: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar. Vanishment contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina’s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice. The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter’s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages – and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: “Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.” Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It’s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he’s selected some great talent to help – guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator.

items.body: Live at Rockpalast 1999 documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm “Mac” Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms. Taped at the height of Dr. John’s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close. A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac’s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
items.label: Mig

items.body: A little before the end of the last century, a revelatory compilation appeared, seemingly from nowhere. From Where I Stand: The Black Experience In Country Music opened a window on something so many didn’t even know existed to show that country music had never been a white preserve. That album was a few years before the Carolina Chocolate Drops burst on the scene, reclaiming the Black heritage in country and string band music, plus a great deal more. Genuine Negro Jig , their third release, saw them move up to the prestigious Nonesuch label, a powerful artistic imprimatur, winning them a Grammy for an album very far removed from the mainstream.

items.body: Lola Amour celebrated a decade of music with a sold-out two-night anniversary event at 123 Block in Mandaluyong on 22 and 23 May, drawing over 2,500 fans across the weekend for a heartfelt full-circle celebration of the band’s journey. Originally planned as a one-night show on 23 May, overwhelming demand prompted the addition of a “Pre-Game” night on 22 May — with both dates eventually selling out. Across the two evenings, fans were treated to performances from Any Name’s Okay, Jan Roberts, Shirebound, and The Ridleys, alongside a career-spanning set from Lola Amour themselves. Beyond the live performances, attendees also explored the Lola Amour Museum, an exhibit showcasing memorabilia from the band’s 10-year history. Among the featured pieces were the band’s 2017 Wanderband Champions trophy, their Japan Ruby Award from the 2025 Music Awards Japan, and the iconic “Shiela” costume from the ‘Raining in Manila’ music video. The anniversary weekend was packed with memorable moments that highlighted the band’s close relationship with its fans and collaborators. One standout performance saw Sof of Any Name’s Okay join the band for ‘Clarity’, while a chaotic and crowd-pleasing cover of ‘Mr. Brightside’ brought together Jan Roberts, Renzo of Any Name’s Okay, Ivo Impreso of PLAYERTWO, and former road manager Peter onstage. During the set, bassist Manu crowd-surfed through the audience, earning one of the loudest cheers of the weekend. Fans also witnessed a playful moment during ‘Lambing’, where frontman Pio transformed into a human disco ball with a mirrored helmet during the song’s instrumental break. The emotional high point of the celebration came during a reunion of the bands that would eventually form Lola Amour. Former members Raymond King and Martin Kim returned to perform as Decaf, while current trumpeter Angelo Mesina briefly returned to his original role as drummer. Joxx Perez and Renzo Santos also made surprise appearances as Sinigang Na Baboy. To close the weekend, all former members joined Lola Amour onstage for the final chorus of ‘Raining in Manila’, creating a powerful moment that encapsulated the band’s decade-long journey from playing small venues to becoming one of the Philippines’ biggest acts. Part concert, part reunion, and part tribute to the community that has supported them since the beginning, Lola Amour’s anniversary weekend felt less like a retrospective and more like a celebration of everything still ahead for the band.
items._cn_summary: Lola Amour是一支来自菲律宾的独立流行摇滚乐队，本次十周年纪念演出以流行摇滚风格为主，呈现了乐队的代表作品及多首合唱曲目。演出加入了变装disco ball、cover表演等娱乐性元素，并邀请其他乐队参与，展现了东南亚独立音乐社群的互动氛围。然而，从音乐风格来看，演出内容偏向主流流行摇滚范畴，编曲结构传统，缺乏实验性声响设计或跨界融合元素，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士、电子、黑暗音乐等方向存在较大差异。尽管演出在本地具有情感号召力，但整体音乐创新性有限，难以满足追求独特艺术视角的听众需求。

items.body: When it comes to music, music videos are important supplements to what we can hear as they stimulate our visual senses in a way that sound cannot. From creative homemade projects to cinematic works that beg to be seen on a big screen, all forms of music videos are released by Singapore's talented musicians seeking to extend the stories told in their songs every month. In this monthly series, we will be rounding up the latest releases from our sunny island that might fly under the radar. Check out Hear65 's guide to local music videos for this month and contact us at hello@hear65.com to submit your music videos! Regina Song - 'Your Charm' Five years in the making, Regina Song 's latest bop was written about the thrill of unexpected attraction. Accompanied by this wonderful music video directed by Gareth Christopher , 'Your Charm' is one of her most playful and uplifting offerings yet, capturing both the giddy rush of a crush and a deeper celebration of individuality. "Honestly, this song means so much more to me than what it meant five years ago. Cause it feels like I let a part of my whimsical self come back. I’m finally getting back into my element," the singer-songwriter shared . SHIGGA SHAY 西阁 ft. pH-1 & JP THE WAVY - 'OK CAN' Built around a hypnotic saxophone loop and powered by multilingual bars, SHIGGA SHAY ’s new single ‘OK CAN’ sees the Singapore rapper link up with Korean hip-hop heavyweight pH-1 and Japanese trailblazer JP THE WAVY for a cross-cultural anthem that feels both effortless and electric. Blending English, Singlish, Mandarin, Malay, Tamil, Korean, Japanese, Thai, and French into one seamless exchange, the track transforms a familiar local phrase into a celebration of identity, rhythm, and connection across Asia’s hip-hop scene. Produced by longtime collaborator superjdoug, ‘OK CAN’ continues SHIGGA SHAY’s mission of bringing hometown stories to a global audience through bold, genre-bending sound. Mary Sue - 'U Wish!' Lifted from his upcoming album Rapihaler , out 19 June , ‘U Wish!’ sees Mary Sue keeping things stripped back and unfussy, letting the bars do the heavy lifting over a captivatingly smooth beat. Filmed at Malaysia’s The Spaceship , the no-frills visual captures the rapper casually performing in the studio, with simple lyric captions foregrounding reflections on trust, ambition, love, and inner conflict. It is intimate without trying too hard — less glossy music video, more late-night session energy, giving the track’s rhythm and thoughtful writing room to breathe. Mary Sue - 'WALAO!' We have Mary Sue yet again, this teaming up with Kuala Lumpur rapped Dametrill . Known for using a blend of Malay, Cantonese, English and Mandarin in his delivery, the mulilingual emcee joins forces with Mary Sue for a captivating track entitled 'WALAO!' . (For those unfamilar "walao” is a Singlish/Malaysian English exclamation with Hokkien roots, used when you’re surprised, annoyed, impressed, frustrated, or reacting strongly to something.) Produced by Atlanta-based underground experimental hip-hop artist feardorian , the song's surge-adjacent beat is a strangely a breezy complement to Mary Sue and Dametrill's Malay Peninsula slang. Shye - 'In The End' Serving as the emotional and melancholic centrepiece of Shye ’s sophomore album The Doves Came Home , ‘In The End’ drifts through shimmering dream-pop textures and towering shoegaze-inspired distortion with a quiet sense of acceptance. Drawing sonic inspiration from Cocteau Twins, Ride, and The Smashing Pumpkins, the track captures the fragile moment of realising that letting go is not a defeat, but a necessary step toward finding your way back to yourself. Anchored by Shye’s airy vocals and introspective songwriting, ‘In The End’ reflects the album’s lingering tension between softness and overwhelm, clarity and uncertainty — ultimately embracing the peace that comes with surrendering to the unknown. Inspired by visions of sunflower fields and the quiet comfort of nature, the song pairs gentle reflection with hope, capturing the desire to “meet yourself halfway” and say the things you once needed to hear. Accompanied by a dreamy self-directed video, the track stands out as one of the brighter moments on the album, with the sunflower emerging as a symbol of resilience, forgiveness, and always turning toward the light. ‘If Today Was Yesterday’ feels like a comforting reminder to hold your younger self a little softer through life’s colder seasons. Shye - 'Someone, Always' ‘Someone, Always ’ is a tender and introspective offering that captures the quiet persistence of love and memory. Also lifted from her sophomore album The Doves Came Home , the track leans into soft, looping thoughts of someone who never quite leaves your mind — “inside your head all the time, everyday” — even in absence. Written, produced, and visualised entirely by Shye , with its accompanying video shot in Manila, the song unfolds like a late-night confession, tracing the spaces between longing and hesitation. Anchored by its recurring question — what is left to say? — ‘Someone, Always’ feels like a gentle push to voice the feelings we often leave unspoken, making it a poignant love letter to the people we carry with us, always. Shohini - 'here for you' Shohini leans into uncomfortable honesty on her new single ‘here for you’ , a heartfelt pop track about the struggle of trusting others and allowing yourself to be vulnerable. Written from a deeply personal place, the song explores avoidant tendencies, emotional walls, and the fear of burdening the people around you — all wrapped in an upbeat, playful energy that keeps things light without losing emotional weight. Through candid lyricism and warm, feel-good production, Shohini hopes ‘here for you’ can offer listeners a sense of comfort, connection, and reassurance that they don’t have to carry everything alone. items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Conceived during the tour for the previous album, Led Zeppelin's second volume is so distinct that it possesses its own autonomy. The approach is more direct, the sound is rawer, the songs seem tailor-made for live performance, and Page's growth as a riff-maker, one of his many facets, encompassing hard rock, blues, and soul, is gradually evident. However, certain litanies, remnants of psychedelia, can detract somewhat from the effectiveness, diverting the focus, as can be seen in "Whole Lotta Love" or "Moby Dick." These disruptions might be justifiable in a live performance, but in the studio version, they diminished the impact of gems that otherwise would have shone even brighter. Beyond this compositional observation, the band was at the height of its creative powers, brimming with ideas, and each member contributing their own unique touch.What Is and What Should Never Be breaks new ground, with jazzy undertones and a fusion of 60s British pop, blues, and funk... all within a song format, with Jimmy Page knowing when to glide peacefully and when to attack with deadly ferocity.Throughout Volume II, John Paul Jones's presence grows enormously, underpinning the foundations of the tracks until he becomes indispensable. Robert Plant had already developed his own style, making his voice another instrument and another flagship of the quartet's sound.The Lemon Song continues as a fundamental building block in what is constructed on this second album, where if it teaches us one lesson, it's that the blues is always something more, a vehicle to add elements and enrich the journey. And John Paul Jones's bass, which one can hear at times in addition to Jimmy's guitar, and the groove achieved were limitless.Led Zeppelin was always more than just good music. Unlike other bands on their contemporaries with similar characteristics, a certain mystical air gradually awakened within them, particularly in Jimmy Page, and that aura was transferred to compositions like "Thank You," music by Page and lyrics by Plant, an instant classic, almost like entering a chapel with muddy boots...guided by John Paul Jones' organ, before returning to the plea in "Heartbreaker," and another immortal guitar riff (not many can say the same). And fundamentally, there was that communion of the group, whose chemistry was at its best, those years when they were like an indivisible unit...recording together, traveling together, eating together, and that translated into the music.With "Living Loving Maid (She's Just A Woman)," they do whatever they want with time and rhythm, constantly changing them, making the song another example of instantaneous change within a song format, stretching and forever altering it. "Ramble On" will be a first approach to that electro-acoustic format that they will fully explore in Volume III, with Plant dressed in one of his many guises, and again the bass roving alongside the guitar, driving the rhythm of the composition. A funky, groovy drum rhythm that becomes Andean-like with guitars on the cliffs, with Page already playing his intricate parts that nevertheless seem simply enchanting in their placidity. And therein lies its charm!They could explode...and they could curl up in a corner...Bring It On Home closes a bluesy album full of contrasts, trying out different outfits and sharpening their weapons for the future...everything was here waiting for the moment to be used...but masters of the stage...lighting only what they wanted to be seen...the quintessence of a band that covered ground with an aerial perspective.
items._cn_summary: 这是Led Zeppelin于1969年发行的第二张专辑，属于硬摇滚与布鲁斯摇滚融合的风格。专辑在当时的摇滚乐坛具有重要地位，展现了Jimmy Page作为 riff 创作者的成长，以及John Paul Jones逐渐关键的贝斯与键盘贡献。乐评详细分析了如《What Is and What Should Never Be》的爵士色彩融合、《The Lemon Song》的布鲁斯实验、《Ramble On》的电声探索等亮点。然而，作为1969年的经典摇滚作品，它与现代实验/前卫/电子/爵士等用户关注的音乐类型存在明显差距。虽然专辑展现了乐队成员间的化学互动与创作活力，但在声音设计的创新性和跨领域融合的实验性上，仍属于传统摇滚范畴，与用户的音乐口味匹配度较低。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Kamelot is certainly one of the most enduring US power metal bands, known for a string of excellentearly 2000s releases and for their progressive-oriented and melodramatic sound. Their recent albums,however, tend to exhibit a dark and dystopian aesthetic that partially reminisces the music of bandslike Symphony X and Circus Maximus. Furthermore, many of their songs have great commercialpotential, and a large number of the songs appearing on 'The Shadow Theory' make no exception, whichis commendable. This is studio album number twelve from Kamelot, and third overall with Swedishvocalist Tommy Karevik, who has more or less become the face of this new era of the band. His voiceis really powerful, and his range is truly impressive, as heard on this very record.As for the album itself, it is a pretty standard-sounding proggy power metal album that combinesbombastic, pompous keyboards and orchestral arrangements with fast-paced guitars, technical riffs,and a strong propensity for memorable (and sometimes corky) melodies and straightforward songstructures. There is not much separating this album from the rest of the band's albums with Karevikas the lead singer, even though some fans have pointed out that this is not necessarily a bad thing.'The Shadow Theory' is a conceptual record, as the lyrics have a lot to do with sci-fi themes, whichis not uncommon for this band. Some key tracks here include 'RavenLight', 'Amnesiac', 'Static' and'MindFall Remedy', although the majority of the songs on here are well-written and well-produced.There is a melodramatic sheen and an indisputable energy that renders Kamelot's music ratherenjoyable. And with this in mind, 'The Shadow Theory' can be a perfect treat for someone who likestheatrical power metal with proggy bits and contemporary production. I personally find some of thewriting a bit shallow and predictable, as the record hardly introduces any new adjustments to theKamelot formula, but the overall impression I get is that of a really well-composed record.
items._cn_summary: KAMELOT的《The Shadow Theory》是2018年发行的一张典型美国力量金属专辑，融合了前卫金属元素与交响编排，呈现出商业化潜力较高的戏剧化风格。专辑为概念性作品，歌词围绕科幻主题展开。作为乐队第十二张专辑和与瑞典主唱Tommy Karevik的第三次合作，作品在编曲上采用了快节奏吉他、技术性 riff 和管弦乐层层叠加的手法。评论者认为这张专辑与乐队此前作品风格一致，缺乏创新性，编曲虽工整但略显可预测。对于偏好实验前卫、爵士、电子等非主流口味的听众而言，这种传统力量金属框架内的作品与用户口味匹配度较低，属于主流商业发行范畴。

Home » Jazz Articles » Album Review » Darryl Alexander: Morning Calls

 LIKE 1
Darryl Alexander: Morning Calls
By La-Faithia White
May 25, 2026
View read count
Jazz artist, producer, and composer Darryl Alexander Sr. began developing his skills as a musician in his school band playing trombone, tuba, and drums. Alexander began his recording career with his debut release titled Coast to Coast (1992) followed by 17th Street (1995), both on the Prestige jazz label. 

"Writing Our Story" opens with a slow, reflective tenor saxophone melody from Jeff Kashiwa. As Ken Karsh enters on rhythm guitar, the composition begins to unfold with a sense of quiet intensity. Momentum builds with the soulful single "Seen It Before."  Jackiem Joyner's soprano saxophone introduces an upbeat groove, supported by Wilbur Krebs on electric bass.  Keyboard and guitar solos from Alexander and Karsh add depth and movement.  "Rise Up" brings a smooth, funky rhythm, with Kenny Blake's alto saxophone delivering a sweet and engaging melody.  Pete Tokar's piano solo blends seamlessly into the track's flow.  

A shift in texture arrives with "Sunset After 7" where Latin-inspired percussion and tropical horn elements create a warm, atmospheric feel.  Soft piano by Alton Merrell.   The track closes with a tasteful acoustic guitar solo by Karsh.  "Didn't See It Coming" stands out as a highlight. Kashiwa and Tokar create a strong musical dialogue, supported by a rich rhythm section. The slow groove allows space for expressive phrasing, culminating in a beautifully controlled ending.   "Wonders of Your Love" offers a mid-tempo ballad featuring Jeff Green on soprano saxophone, complemented by Karsh's subtle guitar work.  

"Intrigued" continues the smooth jazz aesthetic, with Kashiwa delivering a soulful tenor saxophone performance that is both relaxed and expressive.  "High Road" unfolds gradually, with Tokar's piano and Rhodes guiding a winding melodic path that fades gently.   "Almost There" introduces layered textures, combinding Kenny Blake's alto saxophone with Alexander's keyboard work and rhythmic programming. Guitar solo by Karsh and solo by Croes on Rhodes add dimension.  "Pacific Blue" maintains the album's momentum, with Blakes's alto saxophone leading into a groove supported by guitar and Rhodes.  The energy peaks   with "No Middle Ground," where percussion, bass, and saxophone drive an upbeat and confident arrangement.  Karsh's electric guitar solo adds a strong finishing touch.

Morning Calls moves with intention, blending smooth jazz textures with layered insturmentation and collaborative energy. Each track contributes to a narrative shaped by melody, groove, and refined musicianship.  

A few words from Darryl Alexander on the passing of bassist Fred Ervin in December 2025.

While Fred was one of the gifted bassists to grace this planet, his humility and kindness is what marked him the most. He had an infectious smile, loved the Lord, and had an energy and spontaneity that came out in his musical performances. It was a blessing to have a great, long lasting friendship for the majority of our lives. Thank you, Darryl Alexander

items._cn_summary: Morning Calls是一张典型的平滑爵士风格专辑，延续了80-90年代商业爵士的创作范式。专辑以旋律优美、节奏流畅为导向，器乐配置以萨克斯、钢琴、吉他为主，融合拉丁节奏元素但未涉及实验性声响或跨领域融合。各曲目呈现标准化的smooth jazz结构：先是器乐主奏引入旋律，中段加入键盘和吉他solo，最后以整体编配收尾。音乐叙事围绕旋律展开，氛围轻松且易于聆听。整体而言，专辑制作精良、演奏水准扎实，但缺乏创新性视角和实验性表达，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、学院派爵士方向差异明显，属于类型化商业爵士作品。

Home » Jazz Articles » Album Review » Ben Markley Big Band: Tuesday Morning Feeling

 LIKE 3
Ben Markley Big Band: Tuesday Morning Feeling
By Jack Bowers
May 24, 2026
View read count
When a bandleader says he plans to rely less on arranging the music of others to focus more on his own compositions and charts, the usual response is a prolonged sigh or indifferent shrug of the shoulders —which makes it all the more remarkable that when pianist and composer Ben Markley did exactly that on Tuesday Morning Blues, the third recording by the Colorado-based Ben Markley Big Band, the finished product demands not a sigh or shrug but a straight-from-the-heart standing ovation.

Simply put, Tuesday Morning Blues is one of the more colorful and electrifying big-band albums produced in many a moon, and the lion's share of credit for that must be ascribed to Markley's superlative compositions and arrangements. Markley wrote seven of the album's eleven spellbinding numbers, and not one of them is less than compelling and persuasive. The same can be said for the outliers: a brace of originals by Cedar Walton, another by Thelonious Monk, and Willard Robison's durable standard, "Old Folks."

Every composition, of course, needs seasoned musicians to unravel it, and Markley not only assembled a high- quality band comprised of many of Colorado's finest but upped the ante by inviting several world-class artists to lend their invaluable helping hands. Trumpeters Bijon Watson and Terell Stafford answered the call, as did trombonist Steve Davis, vibraphonist Steve Nelson, bassist David Wong and drummer Kyle Swan. To note that their presence makes an appreciable difference would be to understate the reality, as they are an essential part of the album's makeup and persona.

Led by shouting brass (a hallmark of the album as a whole), the band swings out of the starting gate with Markley's plainspoken "Tell the  Truth," a dazzling opener on which Nelson, Markley—whose talents at the keyboard should not be discounted—and Stafford sculpt incisive solos. There is no letdown on Markley's muscular "JIFE" or the luminous and captivating "Ben's Tune," either of which would no doubt merit a place of honor in any big-band library. Swan, guitarist Steve Kovalcheck and alto saxophonist Remy LeBoeuf solo on "JIFE," Markley, Swan and Davis on "Ben's Tune."

Monk's "Off Minor" is a pleasant surprise, prancing straight ahead in Markley's perceptive arrangement while embracing ambitious solos by Nelson and tenor Peter Sommer and setting the stage for the far-from-gloomy "Snowy Range Blues," amplified and bedecked by Nelson, Davis and Stafford, whose lyrical showpiece, the venerable "Old Folks," is next in line. As envisioned by Markley, that "Tuesday Morning Feeling" is luminous and refreshing, as are the deft ad libs by Nelson, Wong and Stafford.

The name "1330" must refer to a train, as the ensemble and Swan mirror the unmistakable sound of a choo-choo in motion at the outset and in an extended coda. Davis solos in the interim, as does alto Wil Swindler, who makes certain his first appearance is one to place in the "noteworthy" column. "NPS," the first of Walton's themes, hurries along a similar track, chugging relentlessly onward behind gutsy solos by Nelson and Stafford, after which Markley invites everyone to "'Mon Back" for one more high-powered blast before invoking once more the essence of Walton for the lively and impressive finale, "Groundwork." Swindler makes his second notable appearance (with Kovalcheck and trumpeter Gabe Mervine), while Stafford, Swan and tenor Jared Caffey share the last words on "Groundwork."

Even though brass and reeds are ascendant on every number, enough good words cannot be said about the band's alert and attentive rhythm section, firmly anchored by Swan and including Markley, Kovalcheck and Wong. With backing like that, it is well nigh impossible to crash or even stumble. Everyone on Tuesday Morning Feeling is in lock-step, and, despite its adamant intensity, there is nary a stray note or clam to be found anywhere in the studio. The album, Markley writes, reflects how he hears a modern big band: "swinging hard, grounded firmly in the tradition, and centered around giving the musicians space to be themselves." Boy, did he ever check all those boxes!

Tuesday Morning Feeling is an astute and collaborative tour de force from start to finish, on Tuesday or any other day. And the album's 78-minute playing time is icing on an already delectable cake.

items.body: Looking back on a glorious 11-year journey, the sun isn't setting anytime soon on SEVENTEEN as they celebrate their anniversary, sharing warm and heartfelt messages with CARATs on Weverse. Earlier this year, S.Coups, Jeonghan, Joshua, Jun, Hoshi, Wonwoo, Woozi, DK, Mingyu, The8, Seungkwan, Vernon, and Dino all renewed their contracts with PLEDIS Entertainment, strengthening their bond with fans as they make a pledge to be their favourite idols for as long as they can. With many more milestone anniversaries on the horizon, CARATs celebrate this landmark moment by sharing clips of old performances and iconic moments that stay etched in their minds. As fans reminisce about the journey of the group so far, the members took to Weverse to share their messages of appreciation, joining in on the nostalgic reflection of the paths they've forged. Although he is currently serving his national service, Hoshi expresses his excitement to complete his duties and reunite with the band to continue performing and creating new bangers for fans to rock out to. The8 echoes a similar sentiment as he expresses his love by saying, "It’s been 11 years. Thank you for always being by our side, thank you to all the members for getting this far, it hasn’t been easy. Because of the time we’ve spent together, we've long become a part of each other’s lives. We hope to continue creating many more memories together in the future. Thank you for your unwavering love." As each member expresses their gratitude for the support from CARATs for the past 11 years, they look forward to an even more eventful future as SEVENTEEN. The group anticipates more new hits, even bigger performances, and new endeavours as they continue to preserve the original energy and passion that they have served up since their debut.

items.body: Filipino-Canadian alt-pop breakout MICO is finally heading to Singapore for his first-ever show in the city. The singer-songwriter will bring his Running From a Feeling Tour to Foo Chow Hall on 19 November for what’s set to be one of his biggest regional performances yet. Presented by LAMC, the upcoming concert arrives fresh off MICO’s sold-out international tour run, with the artist continuing to build momentum through his emotionally driven blend of pop-punk nostalgia and modern alt-pop sounds. Inspired by acts like Fall Out Boy, 5 Seconds of Summer, and The All-American Rejects, MICO has quickly carved out a space for himself with tracks such as ‘HOMESICK’, ‘DREAMBOY’, ‘and cut my hair’. View this post on Instagram A post shared by L.A.M.C. (@lamcpresents) The 23-year-old artist, whose real name is Miguel Veloso, first gained traction through bedroom recordings and online performances before signing with Columbia Records. Since then, he has amassed a devoted fanbase online — affectionately known as “amicos” — while releasing his debut album When the lights turn on. Fans can expect soaring singalongs, heartfelt storytelling, and a cathartic live experience when MICO takes the stage this November. According to the press release, the show will spotlight music from When the lights turn on alongside fan-favourite singles that helped propel the artist’s rise in the alt-pop scene. Tickets (general sales on 28 May) for the Singapore show are priced at S$138 for General Admission, while group bundles for three or more are available at S$128 per ticket. Sign up for pre-sale (27 May) here.

items.body: RIIZE keep their musical momentum going as they soar into a warm and summery new chapter with their upcoming album II, hitting the charts on 15 June. Following the successful release of their debut full-length album ODYSSEY, the sextet explores a new sonic direction with this project, reinforcing their versatility with each release. Spanning six tracks, II is a statement of raw artistic authenticity with a straightforward message that emphasises the importance of staying true to yourself. At the heart of the album is the title track 'Do Your Dance', that doubles down on the key message of the album while blending their signature musicality with layered sonic textures and evocative storytelling through the lyrics. RIIZE empower fans, telling them to own their spotlight with confidence through the signature vocals that have defined the group's sound, delivered with the maturity of a group entering its fourth year. RIIZE unveiled an official schedule detailing each upcoming release as part of the mini album. Fans can look forward to the string of teaser content, including trailer videos and images, a preview of the title track, and music video teasers set for release from 25 May onwards, leading up to the record's release on 15 June. With II, RIIZE continue to cement their place as one of K-pop’s most exciting rising acts, balancing experimentation with the signature sound that fans have come to love. As anticipation builds toward the album’s release, the project promises to usher in another defining era for the group, one fuelled by confidence, growth, and a fearless embrace of their evolving artistry.

items.body: The ball flies toward the goal and Nike scores with their absolutely insane lineup of legendary musicians and sports players for the Universe of Football campaign that launches before the FIFA World Cup 2026. While this year's instalment of the major sports event has had a heavy emphasis on music, with the first-ever halftime shows and multiple theme songs being released, Nike leans into the fusion of sports and music by highlighting stars from each "field" in their campaign. They announced the artists and sports professionals featured in the campaign with a series of autographed Polaroids. Fresh off her electrifying release of the World Cup 2026 anthem 'Goals', BLINKs were sent into a frenzy when they saw their favourite K-pop princess featured in the list of artists. Comments were flooded with love for LISA, with many saying they can't wait for further updates and announcements. The star-studded lineup also featured global heavyweights such as Drake, the ICEMAN keeping it cool with his surprise three-album release, alongside Central Cee, Kim Kardashian, Serena Williams, Cristiano Ronaldo, Travis Scott, Mbappé, and many more. Blending the worlds of music, fashion, and football into one spectacle, Nike’s Universe of Football campaign captures the larger-than-life energy surrounding the upcoming FIFA World Cup 2026. With an all-star cast, the campaign further cements this year’s tournament as not just a sporting event, but a global cultural moment fuelled by entertainment and creativity.

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Black Sabbath's aptly titled 'Vol. 4' is the British metal pioneers' fourth studio album, and once again, it's another release that I struggle to really get into. I don't dislike Black Sabbath, I enjoy most genres of music and most bands, from any era. But for whatever reason, the stars just do not align because I just don't "get" the first few Black Sabbath albums. I'm sure there's a point, perhaps later in their career, where the band just clicks with me, but their first few records, often revered as metal masterpieces by fans, just do nothing for me. It's not all gloom and doom though (well, it kind of is!), as there are a couple of highlights. 'Snowblind' is a fantastic song, probably ranking up there as one of my Sabbath favourites, cheesy ballad 'Changes' has some great vocal and lyrics, and 'St. Vitus Dance' has some interesting guitar work. But overall, I find the rest of the tracks just seem to plod along, similarly to how I felt about their previous releases. I've tried and tried, and have had this one on my playlist for a while, but it's just not working for me. Perhaps I'll have more luck with their next album?

items.album: Jackson Hollow Contemplates Everyday Moments with “A Lovely Day”
items.excerpt: Jackson Hollow has released “A Lovely Day,” the final single from its forthcoming album, Deep Blue Sky, due July 10. Co-written by Rick Lang and…
items.body:
Jackson Hollow has released “A Lovely Day,” the final single from its forthcoming album, Deep Blue Sky, due July 10. Co-written by Rick Lang and labelmate Katelyn Ingardia, the song reflects on gratitude, stillness, and beauty in everyday moments. Its acoustic arrangement highlights the Canadian bluegrass band’s close harmonies, lead vocals, and traditional roots with a modern edge.

The single follows a run of recognition for Jackson Hollow, including a 2024 JUNO Award nomination for Traditional Roots Album of the Year, Canadian Folk Music Award nominations, and a 2025 IBMA Momentum Band of the Year nomination. The band has also reached the Top 3 on the Banjo Radio chart with multiple singles.

Deep Blue Sky continues the group’s focus on storytelling, refined musicianship, and bluegrass tradition. The album also builds on recent honors, including Bluegrass Song of the Year at the Josie Music Awards and Bluegrass Vocalist of the Year for Tianna Lefebvre.

Musicians: Tianna Lefebvre on lead vocals; Mike Sanyshyn in fiddle, mandolin, and harmony vocals; and Charlie Frie on bass and harmony vocals. Guests on the track include Michael Kilby on guitar and dobro, and Justin Moses on banjo.
